course_name_original: Desarrollo de un Prototipo Mecatrónico – Proyecto de Semestre
course_name_en: Development of a Mechatronic Prototype – Semester Project
prerequisites: Knowledge of mechanics, electronics and control at a degree level
Knowledge and skills acquired in the different subjects of the first semester of the master's degree
It is advisable to have successfully passed all subjects of the first semester

learning_outcomes.text: Possess and understand knowledge that provides a basis or opportunity to be original in the development and/or application of ideas, often in a research context.
Students know how to apply the acquired knowledge and their problem-solving ability in new or little-known environments within broader (or multidisciplinary) contexts related to their area of study.

Students are able to integrate knowledge and face the complexity of formulating judgments based on information that, being incomplete or limited, includes reflections on the social and ethical responsibilities linked to the application of their knowledge and judgments.
Students know how to communicate their conclusions and the ultimate knowledge and reasons that support them to specialized and non-specialized audiences clearly and unambiguously.
Students possess the learning skills that allow them to continue studying in a largely self-directed or autonomous way.

Prepare technical specifications that allow a problem in mechatronic engineering to be posed, maintaining a global and integrative vision and using prescriptive, procedural or performance specifications as appropriate.
Organize conceptual design activity to support decision-making and selection among possible solutions to an engineering problem.

Acquire the necessary skills to act as administrators of mechatronic systems design, assuming planning (setting goals and strategies), organization (assigning tasks and resources, coordinating), direction (leading and motivating) and control (monitoring) functions.
Document the specification, implementation and commissioning of mechatronic equipment and systems, taking into account the technical aspects and corresponding regulatory standards.
Develop skills for working in cooperative and multidisciplinary technical teams.
Lead technical teams of specialist engineers in multidisciplinary projects and maintenance of industrial equipment and facilities.
Select the material, dimension and optimize the shape of mechatronic system elements, taking into account resistance, durability and reliability criteria.
Plan the manufacturing processes of the components of a mechatronic system, taking into account the restrictions imposed by the manufacturing, assembly and verification environment.
Plan the assembly, commissioning and maintenance of a mechatronic equipment or system.
Select the most appropriate programmable logic devices in each case for the design of mechatronic systems, manage their development systems and design the interface stages that may be necessary.
Incorporate the necessary electrical, hydraulic and pneumatic sensors and actuators depending on the characteristics of the mechatronic system, its specifications and its integration with it.
Select electronic devices for instrumentation and control that allow conditioning and processing analog and digital signals from sensors and sent to typical actuators of a mechatronic system.
Discriminate the most critical components in a mechatronic system and justify their possible redesign from the point of view of the control system.
Justify in a well-founded way the different options for the automation of a mechatronic machine or technological process.
Acquire knowledge, techniques and skills that imply an increase in research and innovation potential and foster technological transfer to industry.
Apply the knowledge acquired in the design, manufacture and commissioning of mechatronic prototypes.
Be able to work in a group efficiently and coordinately.
Be able to respond to prototype development problems, as well as adapt to unforeseen situations.
Properly manage the manufacture and assembly of the prototype.
Correctly document the technical-economic part of the project carried out.
Present and orally defend the project carried out.

syllabus_topics: Presentation of the problem to be solved.
Proposal of alternatives and selection of alternative to be developed.
Calculations to be made to justify the design.
Assembly and verification of the prototype.
assessment_rules: The asignatura will be evaluated based on oral tests (20%), project (70%), and aptitude scale (10%). Grammar and spelling errors will negatively affect the grade of all submitted documents. Oral tests will be individually assessed and linked to the project, evaluating explanation structure, correct terminology, and technical knowledge. The project will be group-assessed, considering individual contributions, technical content, knowledge structure, and terminology. The extraordinary December-January and differentiated evaluations will be based on oral tests and the project with the same weights; work can be individual or group depending on student numbers.
